content.body:
The Blitzkrieg revealed that the German Army had spent much of the interwar period developing novel ways of fighting war; one of them being the close cooperation between ground and air forces. The converse of this was that the Wehrmacht was acutely aware of how vulnerable ground troops were to air attack. Designed by Rheinmetall, the 20 mm FlaK 30 initially entered production for the Kriegsmarine in 1934 and was not accepted for service by the Luftwaffe until 1935. The FlaK 30 design was that of an over-sized machine gun operating with an open bolt. It was in fact a direct descendant of the MG 30 machinegun. Designed to provide immediate anti-aircraft fire against low-flying attack aircraft, its utility as a heavy infantry support weapon was enhanced by 20 mm AP ammunition. The FlaK 30 was the most widely used 20 mm anti-aircraft weapon in the world by 1940. This light-weight weapon, hampered only by a low rate of fire, saw service throughout the entire war on all fronts where Germany fought.
In Battleground Europe you should deploy this gun to provide a close-in anti-aircraft umbrella over attacking forces. Try to set up in a brush line or in trees behind your main advance, where your HE firepower will not only be useful against enemy aircraft, but can also provide heavy fire support for your advancing infantry and defense against light AFV's. It is slow to limber/unlimber, so it is a good idea to restrict your fire to limit the ability of roaming enemy infantry or vehicles to find you.
The low rate of fire means that you need to save your ammo to concentrate on hitting low angle-off targets. Clip reloading is also slow. Keep careful track of your ammunition status so you do not find yourself facing down an enemy tactical bomber with nothing to shoot.
CREW POSITIONS: 1 Commander 2 Gunner
